FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Fipronil SC is used as an insecticide in agriculture. Fipronil SC is generally manufactured to contain 5.0 percent 
(m/m) of Fipronil. 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 
and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
“Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16145 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


FIPRONIL SUSPENSION CONCENTRATE 
(SC) — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for Fipronil SC. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title 
1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water — Specification 
(third revision) 


2771 (Part 1): Corrugated fibreboard boxes — 


1990 Specification: Part 1 General 
requirements (second revision) 

6940 : 1982 Methods of test for pesticides and 
their formulations (first revision) 

8190 (Part 2): Requirements for packaging of 

1988 pesticides: Part 2 Liquid pesticides 
(second revision) 

9754 : 1981 Specification for high density 
polyethylene containers for packing 
of liquid pesticides (up to 1 litre 
capacity) 

10627 : 1983 Methods for sampling of pesticidal 
formulations 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of a suspension of 
Fipronil technical, in an aqueous phase, together vvith 
suitable formulant(s). 


3.1.2 Fipronil technical shall be employed in the 
formulation of the material. 


3.2 Physical 


The material shall comply with the following physical 
requirements: 


3.2.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of cream to light pale 
yellow coloured suspension, free from extraneous 


matter. It shall readily form a suspension, on dilution 
with water, suitable for spray. 


NOTE — Before sampling to verify product quality, inspect 
the commercial container carefully. On standing, suspension 
concentrates usually develop a concentration gradient from top 
to the bottom of the container. This may even result in the 
appearance of a clear liquid on top and/or sediment on the 
bottom. Therefore, before sampling, homogenize the product 
according to instructions given by the manufacturer or, in the 
absence of such instructions, by gentle shaking of the 
commercial container ( for example, by inverting the closed 
container several times). After this procedure, the container 
should not contain a sticky layer of non-dispersed product at 
the bottom. A suitable and simple method of checking for a 
non-dispersed layer ‘cake’ is by probing with a glass rod. All 
the physical and chemical tests must be carried out on a 
laboratory sample taken after the recommended 
homogenization procedure. 


3.2.2 Pourability 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex A, the residue shall not be more than 5 percent 
(m/m) and rinsed residue shall not be more than 0.50 
percent (m/m). 


3.2.3 Spontaneity of Dispersion 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex B, the spontaneity of dispersion of the material 
shall not be less than 60 percent (m/m). 


3.2.4 Suspensibility 


When determined by the method prescribed in Annex 
C, the suspensibility of the material shall not be less 
than 60 percent (m/m). 


3.2.5 Wet Sieve Test 


Not less than 98 percent by mass of the material shall 
pass through a 45 micron IS sieve when determined 
by method described in 11.1 of IS 6940. 


3.2.6 Persistent Foam 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex D, the persistent foam shall not be more than 
60 ml in 1 min. 


3.2.7 pH of Suspension 


When determined by the method prescribed in Annex 
E, the pH of 1 percent solution in standard hard water 
(342 ppm) shall be between 4.0-8.5. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall comply with the chemical 
requirements given in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


IS 16145 : 2013 


3.3.1 Fipronil Content 


When determined by the prescribed method in 
Annex F, the observed Fipronil content, percent (m/m) 
of any of the samples shall not differ from the declared 
nominal value by more than the percent tolerance limits 
given below: 


Nominal Value, Tolerance Limit, 


percent percent 
Up to 9 +10 
-5 
fth inal 
Above 9 and below 50 +5 757 
value 
50 and above +5 
-3 


3.3.1.1 The actual value of the Fipronil content in the 
formulation shall be calculated to the second decimal 
place and then rounding off to the first decimal place 
before applying the tolerances given in 3.3.1. 


3.3.2 Acidity/Alkalinity 


When tested by the method prescribed in 13.5 of 
IS 6940, the acidity (as H,SO,) or alkalinity (as NaOH) 
of the material shall not be more than 0.5 percent by 
mass, respectively. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in HDPE containers 
conforming to IS 9754. These shall be further packed 
in corrugated fibre board boxes conforming to IS 2771 
(Part 1). The container shall also meet the general 
requirements given in 8190 (Part 2). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly on each container in addition to any other 
information, as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 
c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal Fipronil content, percent (m/m); 


h) Cautionary notice worded as in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


6 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material in bulk quantity 
and/or the retail pack of the formulated product is/are 
offered for inspection, representative sample of the 
material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 10627 and 
if tested within 90 days of its date of manufacture, the 
criteria for conformity shall be that the contents, in 
percent (m/m), shall not be less than the declared 
nominal value. The upper limit for conformity shall 
be the same as those given in 3.3.1. 


When the material is offered for inspection after 90 
days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done as 
prescribed in IS 10627, however, the criteria for 
conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the 
limits of tolerances, as applicable over the declared 
nominal value and given under 3.3.1. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in 3.2.2 
to 3.2.7, 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in the 
tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 16145 : 2013 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 3.2.2) 


DETERMINATION OF POURABILITY 


A-0 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The suspension concentrate is allowed to stand for a 
definite time and the amount remaining in the container 
after a standardized pouring procedure is determined. 
The container is rinsed and the amount then remaining 
is determined. 


A-1 APPARATUS 


A 500 ml stoppered measuring cylinder as per 
following requirements: 


Volume equivalent to | subdivision = 5 ml 
of the scale 

Capacity corresponding to lowest = 50 ml 
graduation mark 

Capacity corresponding to highest = 500 ml 
graduation mark 


Length of scale = 250mm 
Overall height = 39cm 
Diameter of base = 10cm 
Stopper = B34 


NOTE — High density polyethylene bottles, 1 000 ml volume 
and Kilner jars, 700 ml volume, can be used but this must be 
recorded with the result. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


Weigh the empty container along with stopper (W,) 
and add enough of the suspension concentrate taken 


from a recently mixed bulk sample to leave 
approximately 20 percent of the volume of the 
container as ullage. Replace the stopper and reweigh 
the container (W,). Allow the container to stand 
undisturbed for 24 h and then pour out the suspension 
concentrate (see Note 1) for 60 s at an angle of 45° 
and then finally invert the container for 60 s 
(see Note 2). Reweigh the container and stopper 
(W,). 


Add distilled water at 20°C (a volume of 80 percent of 
that of the container) and replace the stopper. Invert 
the container 10 times (see Note 3) and empty the 
container as before and reweigh the container and 
stopper (W,). Calculate the residue (R) and the rinsed 
residue (R,). 


R= Wa Wa) 100 percent 
(W - W.) 

= OEN 100 percent 
(W - W) 


NOTES 

1 The length of the standing period and the temperature should 
be agreed previously. 

2 A square sided container should be held so that a flat side is 
underneath. 

3 The term invert the container means that the container’s 
vertical axis is turned through 180°C and then brought back to 
its original position, the whole operation taking about 2 s. 


ANNEX B 
(Clause 3.2.3) 


DETERMINATION OF SPONTANEITY OF DISPERSION 


B-0 OUTLINE OF METHOD 


The method is broadly similar to that used to determine 
the suspensibility of concentrates. It involves preparing 
900 ml of a mixture of formulation and standard hard 
water (342 ppm). After standing under defined 
conditions the top nine-tenths is removed, and the 
remaining tenth assayed chemically, gravimetrically. 
The spontaneity of dispersion is readily calculated. 


B-1 REAGENTS 


B-1.1 Standard Hard Water (342 ppm) — Prepared 
as indicated in 11.2.2.1 of IS 6940. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 Graduated Cylinders — Glass stoppered, 
250 ml capacity. 


IS 16145 : 2013 


B-2.2 Glass Suction Tubes — About 40 cm long, 
5 mm internal diameter, drawn out at one end to 2-3 
mm Internal diameter. 


B-2.4 Magnetic Stirrer 
B-2.5 Rotary Vacuum Evaporator 
B-2.6 Standard Glassware 


B-3 PROCEDURE 


Take 900 ml standard hard water (342 ppm) in a beaker. 
Keep the beaker on magnetic stirrer. Add 8.8 g to 9.2 g 


the suspension. Determine by gravimetric means the 
solid obtained in the remaining 90 ml in the beaker. 
This can be done most conveniently by evaporating 
the liquid in the rotary vacuum evaporator and drying 
to constant weight. 


B-4 CALCULATION 


Calculate the spontaneity of dispersion as per following 
equation: 


M-W am 


Spontaneity of dispersion, percent = 


of sample in the stirred water and continue the stirring where 
for 1 min. Then switch off the stirrer and allow the : 32 
suspension to stand undisturbed for 5 min. Withdraw, W = mass of residue after drying, in g, and 
by means of a vacuum pump, nine-tenth (810 ml) of M = mass of sample taken in g. 
ANNEX C 
(Clause 3.2.4) 


DETERMINATION OF SUSPENSIBILITY 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


Suspensibility of Fipronil is determined by high 
performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) unit 
equipped with UV detector using internal standard 
technique. 


C-2 APPARATUS 


C-2.1 A High Performance Liquid Chromatography 
(HPLC) system equipped with UV-VIS detector and 
chromatographic software/printer plotter-cum- 
integrator or PC based data system. The suggested 
Operative parameters are as follows, but can be 
changed, if necessary, provided standardization is done: 


Column : Stainless steel, 25 cm x 4.6 
mm i.d., packed with C 18, 
Sum 

Temperature : Ambient 

Mobile phase : Acetonitrile: Water (70 : 30 
v/v) 

Flow rate : 1.0 ml/min 

Injection volume : 20 ul 


Detector : Ultraviolet detector (280 nm) 


C-2.2 Analytical Balance 
C-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 25 ul capacity 


C-2.3 Magnetic Stirrer 
C-2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 
C-2.5 Standard Glassware 


C-3 REAGENTS 

C-3.1 Fipronil Reference Standard — of known 
purity. 

C-3.2 Acetonitrile — AR grade, or equivalent. 
C-3.3 Water — AR grade, or equivalent. 


C-4 PROCEDURE 


C-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix acetonitrile and vvater in the proportion of 70 : 30 
(v/v) and pass through membrane filter under vacuum. 
Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic stirrer and 
allovv to attain room temperature. 


NOTE — Dissolution of acetonitrile in vvater is endothermic, 
hence allow the mixing to start at ambient temperature and 
continue till it attains room temperature. 


C-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


VVeigh accurately 0.1 g of Fipronil analytical standard 
of knovvn purity into 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 50 
ml of acetonitrile and dissolve content manually by 


shaking, and sonicate for 15 min. Allow it to attain 
room temperature and make up the volume upto the 
mark with acetonitrile. Call this as Solution ‘A’. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of Solution ‘A’ into a 50 ml 
volumetric flask and make up the volume upto the mark 
with mobile phase and homogenize. Call this as 
Solution “B”. 


C-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution for 
Suspensibility 


Accurately vveigh 1 g of the sample. Perform the 
suspensibility test as per 11.2 of IS 6940. 


Transfer the material at the bottom of the cylinder into 
a 100 ml volumetric flask. Rinse the cylinder with 10 
ml of acetonitrile and transfer the washings to the 
volumetric flask. Sonicate, and make up the volume 
upto the mark with acetonitrile. Filter the solution 
through Whatman filter paper No. 1.

ANNEX D 
(Clause 3.2.6) 


DETERMINATION OF PERSISTENT FOAM 


D-0 SCOPE 


The method is suitable for determining the foam 
created when suspension concentrates are diluted. 


D-1 OUTLINE OF METHOD 


The suspension concentrate is diluted in a measuring 
cylinder of standard dimensions which is inverted 30 
times and the amount of foam created and remaining 


after certain times is measured. 
D-2 REAGENT 
D-2.1 Standard Hard Water 


D-3 APPARATUS 


D-3.1 Graduated Cylinder— Glass stoppered, 
250 ml capacity with 2 ml graduations. The distance 


IS 16145 : 2013 


between the 0 mark and the 250 ml mark should be 20 
cm to 21.5 cm. The distance between the 250 ml mark 
and the bottom of the stopper should be 6 cm to 8 cm. 


NOTE — The cylinder should be clean and free from grease. 


D-3.2 Stopwatch 


D-4 PROCEDURE 


The mass of sample to be taken is that mass required 
to make 200 ml of a suspension with a concentration 
recommended in the directions for use supplied with 
the product. Where several concentrations are 
recommended, the maximum concentration shall be 
used. 


Put about 180 ml of standard hard water into the 250 
ml measuring cylinder kept on a top pan balance and 
weigh in the required amount of suspension 


concentrate (in this case | g of Fipronil 5 percent SC). 
Top up with standard hard water up to 200 ml mark. 
Stopper the cylinder and invert 30 times (see Note 1). 
Place the stoppered cylinder upright on the bench and 
immediately start the stopwatch. Read the volume of 
foam produced and remaining after 1 min 
(see Note 2). 


NOTES 


1 The expression ‘invert the cylinder’ means that the stoppered 
cylinder is held by 2 hands, one at each end of the cylinder, 
which are insulated from the cylinder by means of a cloth. The 
upright cylinder is turned through 180°C and back to its original 
position without any ‘bounce’ occurring, this operation taking 
approximately 2 s. It is convenient to observe a stop-clock 
equipped with a second hand which sweeps once every 60 s 
while doing this. 

2 A few bubbles round the periphery are not significant. Any 
volumes above the 250 ml mark should be marked on the 
outside and the volume of foam thus determined. 


ANNEX E 
(Clause 3.2.7) 


DETERMINATION OF pH OF SUSPENSION 


E-1 PRINCIPLE 


The pH is determined using a pH meter having a range 
0-14 with a precision of 0.1 pH. 


E-2 APPARATUS 


E-2.1 pH Meter — Direct reading, with glass electrode 
and a calomel reference electrode or any other suitable 
electrode along with temperature compensation. 


E-2.2 Balance (Analytical) — Sensitive to 0.1 g. 
E-2.3 Standard Glassware 
E-2.4 Wash Bottle — Containing distilled water. 


E-3 REAGENTS 


E-3.1 Standard Hard Water 


E-3.2 Buffer Tablets — Tablets of pH 4.0, 7.0 
and 9.2. 


E-4 PROCEDURE 


From the buffer tablets, prepare 4.0, 7.0 and 9.2 pH 
buffer solutions, following the prescribed instruction 
given with the tablets. Standardize the pH meter using 
the buffers as follows: 


Immerse the electrodes of the pH meter in 7.0 pH buffer 
solution and adjust the meter to read 7.0 pH. Remove 
the buffer solution from the electrodes, wash these with 
water and wipe the electrodes free from water. 


Replace with pH buffer solution 9.2 and adjust the 
meter to read 9.2 pH. Remove the buffer solution from 
the electrodes, wash these with water and wipe the 
electrodes free from water. Repeat the above procedure 
using 4.0 pH buffer solution. 


Weigh accurately about 1.0 g of the sample and add 
100 ml of standard hard water. Mix the sample 
thoroughly to get a uniform suspension in a beaker. 
Measure the pH of the suspension. Report result to 
nearest 0.1 pH. 


IS 16145 : 2013 


ANNEX F 
(Clause 3.3.1) 


DETERMINATION OF FIPRONIL CONTENT 


F-1 PRINCIPLE 


The Fipronil content is determined by high 
performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) equipped 
with UV detector using external standard technique. 


F-2 APPARATUS 


F-2.1 A High Performance Liquid Chromatography 
system equipped with ultraviolet detector and 
chromatographic software/printer plotter-cum- 
integrator or PC based data system is used for this 
determination. The suggested operative parameters are 
as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided 
standardization is done: 


Column : Stainless steel, 25 cm x 4.6 
mm i.d., packed with C 18, 
Sum 

Temperature : Ambient 

Mobile phase : Acetonitrile: Water (70 : 30 
v/v) 

Flow rate : 1.0 ml/min 

Injection volume : 20 ul 


Detector : Ultraviolet detector (280 nm) 


A typical HPLC chromatogram of Fipronil is given in 
Fig. | 


F-2.2 Analytical Balance 

F-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 25 ul capacity. 
F-2.3 Magnetic Stirrer 

F-2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 

F-2.5 Standard Glassware 


F-3 REAGENTS 


F-3.1 Fipronil Reference Standard — of known 
purity. 


F-3.2 Acetonitrile — AR grade, or equivalent. 
F-3.3 Water — AR grade, or equivalent. 


F-4 PROCEDURE 


F-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix acetonitrile and water in the proportion of 70 : 30 
(v/v) and pass through membrane filter under vacuum. 
Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic stirrer and 


allow it to attain room temperature. 


NOTE — Dissolution of acetonitrile in water is endothermic, 
hence allow the mixing to start at ambient temperature and 
continue till it attains room temperature. 


F-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.1 g of fipronil analytical standard 
of known purity into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 
50 ml of acetonitrile and dissolve content manually by 
shaking and sonicate for 15 min. Allow it to attain room 
temperature and make up the volume upto the mark 
with acetonitrile. Call this as solution ‘A’. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of solution ‘A’ into a 50 ml volumetric 
flask and make up the volume upto the mark with 
mobile phase and homogenize. Call this as solution ‘B’. 


F-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately a quantity of a sample equivalent 
to 0.1 g of Fipronil (approximately 2 g of sample) into 
a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 2.5 ml of water. Keep 
the flask for 10 min and make up the volume upto the 
mark with acetonitrile. Call this as solution ‘C’. 


Pipette out 5 ml of the solution ‘C’ into another 50 ml 
volumetric flask. Make up the volume upto the mark 
with acetonitrile. Shake well to homogenize. Call this 
as solution “D”. 


F-5 ESTIMATION 


Inject 20 ul standard solutions until the area quotients 
of reference standard solution/sample solution of two 
successive chromatograms do not deviate from each 
other by more than 2 percent. Then use the following 
injection sequence: 


... C, S, CS, Ci S; C, S, 


where 
C = standard solution, and 
S = sample solution (1, 2..., n) 


From the chromatograms of standard solution and 

sample solution measure the peak areas of Fipronil and 

calculate the Fipronil content in the suspension as given 

in F-6. 

F-6 RETENTION TIME (GUIDE VALUES) 
Fipronil = 6.0 min (approximately) 


Total runtime = 10min

MINUTES
